commitResults.messageTitle: Update UG and DG for delete by UUID
commitResults.messageBody:
Document the UUID-based delete syntax, example and error cases in the UG,
and update the DG command description, use case UC3, manual testing steps
and the affected sequence/state diagrams. Remove references to deleting
by index.

Fixes #71
Add delete by short UUID
Remove index-based deletion
Update UG and DG for delete by UUID

A hand-edited or corrupted data file can contain a uuid that is not a
valid UUID. UUID.fromString then throws an unchecked
IllegalArgumentException, which escapes the usual IllegalValueException
handling for invalid fields. It also silently accepts shortened forms
such as "1-1-1-1-1".

Check the stored uuid against the canonical 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal form
and throw IllegalValueException when it does not match, so a bad uuid
is reported like any other invalid field.

Log when a legacy save without a uuid is given a fresh one.

The short UUID length of 7 is hard-coded in three places: the
substring in Person#getShortUuid, the delete parser's regex and the
delete usage message. Changing the length means finding and updating
every copy, and missing one makes the card and the parser disagree.

Define the length once as Person.SHORT_UUID_LENGTH and use it
everywhere.

commitResults.messageTitle: Gradle: Enable assertions when running the app
commitResults.messageBody:
Assertions are disabled by default in the JVM, so assert statements
are skipped when the app is launched with gradle run and violated
assumptions go unnoticed.

Enable them for the run task, as required for v1.4.

commitResults.messageTitle: Gradle: Add JUnit parameterized tests dependency
commitResults.messageBody:
Tests that run the same check over many inputs are currently written
as near-identical copies, one per input, which the code quality
guidelines flag as duplication.

Add junit-jupiter-params so such tests can use @ParameterizedTest.

Two persons can share the 7-character short UUID shown on their
cards. The delete command then asks for a more specific identifier,
but it accepts exactly 7 characters, so neither person can be
deleted. The error also does not show the user what to type.

Accept any UUID prefix from 7 to 32 hexadecimal characters, ignoring
dashes, so that a full UUID copied from the data file also works.
When several persons match, list each one's full UUID and name so
the user can see how many characters tell them apart.

Move prefix matching into Person#hasUuidPrefix, and split the lookup
in DeleteCommand into its own method with logging and an assertion.
Use parameterized tests and shared helpers in the delete tests to
remove near-duplicate test cases.

JsonAdaptedPersonTest checks that a malformed uuid is rejected, but
nothing checks that the rejection reaches the storage layer as a
DataLoadingException, which is what lets the app start with an empty
address book instead of crashing.

Add a data file with a malformed uuid and check that reading it
throws DataLoadingException.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add undelete command to restore deleted persons
commitResults.messageBody:
A deleted person is gone for good, so an agent who deletes the wrong
client by mistake has to re-enter every detail by hand, and the
client gets a new UUID.

Add an undelete command that restores the most recently deleted
person, keeping their UUID, at the position they were deleted from.
Repeating it walks further back through this session's deletes.

The model keeps the deleted persons and their indexes in a stack for
the session only. Undelete refuses to restore a person who already
exists, e.g. after being re-added by hand, and keeps them on the
stack so nothing is lost. It takes no arguments, and rejects any, so
it cannot be mistaken for a delete.

commitResults.messageBody: Use short UUIDs to identify people consistently with the remark command and allow edit to update or clear remarks. Replace generic edit target errors with actionable UUID guidance and document the revised syntax.

commitResults.messageTitle: Support dashed UUID prefixes in edit command
commitResults.messageBody: Edit currently accepts only seven-character UUID prefixes, which prevents users from using longer prefixes or full UUIDs copied from the data file.\n\nNormalize dashes and case before validating edit targets, and accept prefixes from seven to 32 hexadecimal characters.

The edit UUID validation and remark-aware descriptor equality paths lack direct tests, leaving recently changed behavior less protected.\n\nAdd invalid UUID constructor cases and a descriptor equality case with differing remarks to exercise these paths.
